brief:
Australia is moving toward adopting formal definitions of racism, including antisemitism, following the Bondi Beach attack, according to Mondoweiss. The initiative has drawn criticism from opponents who argue it aims to criminalize anti-Zionism and advance settler colonialism under the guise of combating discrimination.

The proposed framework would legally define antisemitism in ways that critics say conflate criticism of Israel with hatred of Jewish people. Supporters of the definitions argue they protect against bigotry, while detractors contend the language would effectively criminalize political opposition to Israeli government policies and territorial practices. The debate reflects broader disagreements over how to distinguish between legitimate political speech and hate speech in discussions of the Israeli-Palestinian conflict.
dek: In response to the Bondi Beach attack, there is a push in Australia to adopt definitions of racism, including antisemitism. We must reject this effort because its ultimate goal is to criminalize anti-Zionism and to further settler colonialism.
title: Australia pushes racism definitions tied to antisemitism law.
